url_citation.content:
In Praise of Shadows
IN PRAISE
Foreword by Charles Moore Afterword by Thomas J. Harper
OF SHADOWS Jun’ichird Tanizaki
Translated by Thomas J. Harper and Edward G. Seidensticker
LEETE’S ISLAND BOOKS $b
English translation, Foreword, and Afterword copyright © 1977 by Leete’s Island Books, Inc.
Sixth printing
Library of Congress Catalogue Number 77-75035 ISBN 0-918172-02
Published by Leete’s Island Books, Inc. Box 3131
Stony Creek, CT. 06405 Manufactured in the United States of America
Design by Susan McCrillis Kelsey
This essay has been made available to Leete’s Island Books with the gracious permission of Mrs. Jun ‘ichird Tanizaki.

...

the sun, our staunchest ally, bathing our world or flickering through it, helping give it light.
It comes with the thrill of a slap for us then to hear praise of shadows and darkness; so it is when there comes to us the excitement of realizing that musicians everywhere make their sounds to capture silence or that architects develop complex shapes just to envelop empty space. Thus darkness illuminates for us a cul- ture very different from our own; but at the same time it helps us to look deep into ourselves to our own in- habitation of our world, as it describes with spine- tingling insights the traditional Japanese inhabitation of theirs. It could change our lives.
Charles Moore School of Architecture, UCLA
In Praise of Shadows
